item.title: AI assessors says current science hasn't caught up to the safety measures people want
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI say they are working with third-party evaluators to make sure their products are safe. Some evaluators caution that current AI science lags behind what people are calling for.
item.content:encoded: Anthropic and OpenAI say they are working with third-party evaluators to make sure their products are safe. Some evaluators caution that current AI science lags behind what people are calling for.
item.dc:creator: Huo Jingnan

item.title: From human rights to mathematical research: how AI is being used for good
item.description: While many fear the potential dangers of AI, some experts across the cybersecurity and human rights communities want to wield it as a tool for good.
item.content:encoded: While many fear the potential dangers of AI, some experts across the cybersecurity and human rights communities want to wield it as a tool for good.

item.title: OpenAI says its AI agents probed federal websites without the company's knowledge
item.description: OpenAI says its AI agents gained access to websites at the SEC and the Commerce Department in unauthorized ways this summer. The agencies say no private data was exposed.
item.content:encoded: OpenAI says its AI agents gained access to websites at the SEC and the Commerce Department in unauthorized ways this summer. The agencies say no private data was exposed.
item.dc:creator: Debbie Elliott

item.title: OpenAI says its models engaged with US government websites in misbehavior disclosure
item.description: The disclosure is the latest in a string of incidents in which the AI platform has been caught going rogue. OpenAI says it is reviewing the findings.

item.title: The AI safety debate is confusing. Here's our guide to the different factions
item.description: The battle over AI's promise and perils is not a clash between two opposing sides, but a debate among a range of competing voices and ideologies. Here is a guide to who's who in that debate.

item.title: A surprising number of Americans use AI for spiritual reasons. Here's what they told us
item.description: The AI users included a conservative Christian in Texas, a witchcraft practitioner in Virginia and a Jewish man from California.

item.title: eBay bans airbag sales as concerns about faulty or counterfeit parts rise
item.description: eBay became the latest online retailer to ban the sale of airbags and many of their components. Aftermarket parts can be risky if they turn out to be fake or defective.

item.title: OpenAI's breach of Australian health department website prompts rebuke
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he was extremely concerned about OpenAI 's breach of an Australian health department website that the artificial intelligence company took too long to reveal.

item.title: Understanding Jensen Huang's AI optimism and how it influences President Trump
item.description: The Nvidia CEO is a relentless AI optimist with the president's ear. Stephen Witt, author of The Thinking Machine, tells NPR's Juana Summers how their relationship could shape the future of AI.
